correctness.rationale: For each base b>=2 and modulus m=b+1, the digit sum on the length-b block I_q=[bq,bq+b-1] equals s_b(q)+r, r=0,...,b-1, so precisely one residue class mod m is missing and a full block is zero-free iff s_b(q)=1 mod m. The consecutive-block carry difference is 1-(b-1)t=1+2t mod m where t counts trailing maximal digits. When b is odd (m even) this cannot be zero, so no adjacent good blocks; when b is even three good blocks would force an ordinary +1 transition and are impossible. Interval containment of complete blocks gives L<=3b-2 or 4b-2, and the explicit base-one interval or q=b^(b/2)-1 construction meets each bound. Extremal equality forces start congruent 1 mod b and outside partial blocks residues 0 and 2, yielding the exactly three disjoint odd-base valuation cases and the one even-base carry congruence t=b/2 mod m. For densities, nontrivial Fourier characters of unrestricted high base-b digits decay, even after fixing the last digit, giving s_b(h) mod m uniform on the relevant higher-digit sets; summing the geometric exact-valuation tails yields the displayed closed formulas. An independent program checked all starting positions 1<=a<50000 and length-(L+1) failures for b=2,...,8, and the condition at every tested a; the b=2,3,4,... maximum lengths were 6,7,14,13,22,19,30. This bounded test does not prove any all-base statement or limiting density.
residual_risks: The modulus is specifically b+1, not arbitrary m.
Natural density proof requires the conditional digit-sum Fourier argument and tail truncation; finite frequencies are not the limiting proof.

value.rationale: The modulus b+1 is natural because each full base-b digit block misses exactly one residue class. The theorem resolves the associated sharp interval avoidance problem in every integer base, identifies a genuine parity transition, classifies all extremal starting integers by their carry valuations and determines exact positive natural densities of those rare starts. This is not a substituted version of the decimal 38 result: the odd/even-base mechanisms and frequency constants require additional reasoning and quantify scarcity beyond an isolated maximum.
residual_risks: No claim for general moduli independent of b, or for exact finite-cutoff enumeration of starts.

limitations: Only modulus m=b+1; the values in decimal b10 were in part known and are not claimed new.
Limit densities exist but no exact finite-N count formula is asserted.
